reading.body:
Every tool in this category is capable of autonomous response, meaning the AI can act on threats without waiting for a human decision, and most also hold high-privilege or administrative access to the systems they protect.

That combination, autonomous action plus privileged access, is the defining characteristic of security and identity AI as represented here. Five of the six vendors are US-domiciled; one, Darktrace, is UK-hosted and flagged as GDPR-relevant, which signals that data residency and regulatory jurisdiction are live considerations in this category even when the underlying capability is similar. The tools span endpoint protection, network security, identity management, cloud traffic inspection, and data loss prevention, so the autonomous-response property appears across the full stack, not in one narrow segment.

The data does not include deployment scale, inference compute requirements, or energy load, so no direct connection to power or grid constraint can be drawn from it. What the data does show is that security AI is being granted decision-making authority over critical infrastructure, privileged accounts, and network access, roles that historically required human sign-off. The risk profile of a model error or adversarial manipulation is therefore higher here than in most other AI tool categories, and the data notes kill-switch capabilities for at least one platform, which implies vendors are already designing for the possibility that autonomous action needs to be stopped fast.
